# Lab 23.6: Enable & Query Data Access Logs

## What We Are Going to Do
Turn on Data Access audit logs for Cloud Storage, read an object, and find exactly who read it.

## Steps

1. **Check the default.** Go to **IAM & Admin → Audit Logs**. Most services show Data Access logs off.

2. **Turn them on for Cloud Storage.** Tick **Google Cloud Storage**, then in the side panel tick **Data Read** and **Data Write**. Save.

   The same setting lives in the IAM policy as `auditConfigs`:


<div style="margin:18px 0;border:1px solid #334155;border-radius:8px;overflow:hidden;">
<div style="background:#243244;color:#DBEAFE;padding:7px 12px;font-family:Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:12px;font-weight:700;">
CODE • YAML
</div>
<pre style="margin:0;background:#111827;color:#F3F4F6;padding:16px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;font-family:Consolas,'Cascadia Code',monospace;font-size:14px;line-height:1.55;"><code><span style="color:#F3F4F6;">auditConfigs:
- service: storage.googleapis.com
  auditLogConfigs:
  - logType: DATA_READ
  - logType: DATA_WRITE</span>
</code></pre>
</div>


3. **Generate activity.**


<div style="margin:18px 0;border:1px solid #334155;border-radius:8px;overflow:hidden;">
<div style="background:#243244;color:#DBEAFE;padding:7px 12px;font-family:Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:12px;font-weight:700;">
CODE • BASH
</div>
<pre style="margin:0;background:#111827;color:#F3F4F6;padding:16px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;font-family:Consolas,'Cascadia Code',monospace;font-size:14px;line-height:1.55;"><code><span style="color:#F3F4F6;">gcloud storage buckets create gs://$PROJECT_ID-dal --location=us-central1
echo "sensitive" | gcloud storage cp - gs://$PROJECT_ID-dal/payroll.txt
gcloud storage cat gs://$PROJECT_ID-dal/payroll.txt</span>
</code></pre>
</div>


4. **Query the logs.** You need **Private Logs Viewer** to see Data Access logs.


<div style="margin:18px 0;border:1px solid #334155;border-radius:8px;overflow:hidden;">
<div style="background:#243244;color:#DBEAFE;padding:7px 12px;font-family:Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:12px;font-weight:700;">
CODE • BASH
</div>
<pre style="margin:0;background:#111827;color:#F3F4F6;padding:16px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;font-family:Consolas,'Cascadia Code',monospace;font-size:14px;line-height:1.55;"><code><span style="color:#F3F4F6;">gcloud logging read \
  'logName="projects/'$PROJECT_ID'/logs/cloudaudit.googleapis.com%2Fdata_access" AND protoPayload.resourceName:"payroll.txt"' \
  --limit=5 \
  --format="table(timestamp,protoPayload.authenticationInfo.principalEmail,protoPayload.methodName)"</span>
</code></pre>
</div>


   You see `storage.objects.create` and `storage.objects.get` with your email.

5. **Exempt a noisy principal.** In the Audit Logs panel, open **Exempted principals** and add a service account that reads the bucket thousands of times a day.

6. **Clean up.** Turn off the Data Access logs if you do not need them, then:


<div style="margin:18px 0;border:1px solid #334155;border-radius:8px;overflow:hidden;">
<div style="background:#243244;color:#DBEAFE;padding:7px 12px;font-family:Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:12px;font-weight:700;">
CODE • BASH
</div>
<pre style="margin:0;background:#111827;color:#F3F4F6;padding:16px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;font-family:Consolas,'Cascadia Code',monospace;font-size:14px;line-height:1.55;"><code><span style="color:#F3F4F6;">gcloud storage rm --recursive gs://$PROJECT_ID-dal</span>
</code></pre>
</div>


## Expected Result

| Thing | Reality |
|---|---|
| Default | Off for most services, on for BigQuery |
| After enabling | Every read and write logged |
| Viewer role | Private Logs Viewer needed |
| Cost | Charged per GB, so enable where needed |
